name: BH1750
full_name: ROHM BH1750FVI Digital Ambient Light Sensor (GY-302 breakout)
description: Digital 16-bit ambient light sensor with an I2C interface that outputs illuminance directly in lux, removing host-side calculation. It has a range of roughly 1 to 65535 lx with selectable high/low resolution modes (down to 0.5 lx), and a spectral response close to the human eye. Its built-in ADC and low IR influence suit display backlight control. The common GY-302 breakout adds a 3.3 V regulator and I2C pull-ups so it works from a 3.3-5 V supply.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: supply; GY-302 accepts 3.3-5 V (BH1750FVI chip VDD is 2.4-3.6 V)

typical_application: Display/keypad backlight auto-brightness, light-level logging, plant/grow-light monitoring, ambient light feedback in cameras and IoT nodes.
gotchas: the ADDR pin sets the 7-bit I2C address: low/floating = 0x23 (default), tied high to VCC = 0x5C
the bare BH1750FVI is a 3.x V part (VDD 2.4-3.6 V); only the GY-302 board's regulator makes 5 V safe
it reports lux directly but you must apply the measurement-time (MTreg) scaling factor for accuracy if you change it
the DVI pin on the bare chip is the interface logic reset/reference; on the GY-302 it is exposed as ADDR - do not confuse with a separate reset
a measurement is not instantaneous: H-resolution mode takes ~120 ms, so poll after the conversion time or readings are stale
ADDR left floating reads as low (0x23); to use two sensors on one bus, pull one ADDR high for 0x5C
